title: Comparison of complex executive functions pre- vs. post-after neurosurgical surgery intervention in patients with focal temporal and frontal epilepsy
summary: Large epileptic seizures are characterized by a spread of epileptic brain activity over large areas of the brain. It is not sufficiently known whether and to what extent cognitive performance, which usually depends on intact brain regions, is affected by epileptic activity in other regions even outside the acute seizure event. Brain surgery to remove the tissue presumably causing the epilepsy could therefore have positive consequences for performance if it prevents interference of epileptic activity with other brain regions. The study therefore compares the performance of patients with epilepsy shortly before and 1 year after brain surgery to remove the tissue suspected of causing the epilepsy with the change in complex thinking performance of healthy participants at the same time interval. In addition, patients who have undergone surgery on different regions of the brain will be compared. In order to be able to assess possible cognitive changes to changes in the neuronal system, brain activation measurements using multichannel near-infrared spectroscopy will also be performed at the respective test appointments. We hope that the study will help us to better understand the consequences of epileptic seizures and the brain surgery they cause on mental performance.
conditions: Localization-related (focal)(partial) symptomatic epilepsy and epileptic syndromes with simple partial seizures
Localization-related (focal)(partial) symptomatic epilepsy and epileptic syndromes with complex partial seizures
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Unilateral focal frontal or temporal lobe epilepsy; sufficient physical condition (normal vision or corrected; ability to perform the hand and arm movements necessary for test assessment); ability to understand test instructions; consent is required
Exclusion criteria:
Limited or no inability to understand instruction (e.g. due to limited knowledge of German); neurological disorders (except epilepsy in patients); severe psychiatric disorders (especially acute moderate to severe depressive episode); currently no psychoactive medication (except in the context of epilepsy treatment in patients); participation in other studies with the same test procedures shortly before (6 months) or within the individual study period (avoidance of learning effects)
